course_name: Mathematical Analysis. Part 2. Differential and Integral Calculus of Functions of Several Variables

course_profile.one_sentence_summary: A foundational mathematical analysis course focusing on integral calculus, multivariable calculus, and infinite series for software engineering students.
course_profile.short_summary: This course represents the second part of a comprehensive Mathematical Analysis sequence. It covers indefinite and definite integrals with geometric applications, differential and integral calculus for functions of multiple variables (including partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and optimization), and the theory of numerical and power series (including Taylor and Maclaurin expansions). The course aims to develop logical thinking and provide the mathematical foundation necessary for advanced computer science topics.

theoretical_understanding: Understand the concepts of indefinite and definite integrals, including their geometric and physical meanings.
Understand limits, continuity, and differentiability of multivariable functions.
Understand the theory behind double and triple integrals and coordinate system transformations.
Understand the convergence criteria for numerical and power series.
practical_implementation: Compute indefinite integrals using substitution, parts, and partial fractions.
Evaluate definite integrals using the Newton-Leibniz formula.
Calculate partial derivatives, total differentials, and tangent planes for multivariable functions.
Evaluate double and triple integrals in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates.
analysis_validation: Analyze functions of multiple variables to find local, global, and conditional extrema.
Determine the absolute and conditional convergence of alternating series using Leibniz's theorem.
Determine the radius and interval of convergence for power series.
research_and_prototyping: Apply power series (Taylor and Maclaurin) for approximate calculations of functions.

lab_formats: Independent computational assignments (Типова розрахункова робота - РР)
expected_artifacts: Calculation Work (РР) submitted in parts matching the modules
implementation_tasks: Solving integration problems (rational, trigonometric, irrational functions)
Calculating areas, volumes, and arc lengths manually
engineering_practices: Application of mathematical models to geometric and physical scenarios

curricular_relations.reason: Integration is the inverse operation of differentiation; knowing derivatives is strictly required to find antiderivatives.
The Newton-Leibniz formula requires finding the indefinite integral (antiderivative) to evaluate the definite integral.
Definite integrals are directly applied to compute areas, volumes, and arc lengths.
Partial derivatives extend the rules of single-variable differentiation to functions of multiple variables.
Finding critical points for optimization requires computing first and second-order partial derivatives.
Double and triple integrals are evaluated by iterating single definite integrals.

what_student_can_understand: The fundamental theorem of calculus and the relationship between derivatives and integrals.
The spatial behavior of functions with multiple variables.
The mathematical principles of infinite series and their convergence.
How continuous functions can be represented and approximated by infinite polynomials.
what_student_can_build: Mathematical models for evaluating the volume, surface area, and arc length of complex geometries.
Optimization setups to find maximum and minimum values of multivariable systems under specific constraints.
what_student_can_apply: Integration techniques to solve applied physical and geometric problems.
Taylor series to create polynomial approximations of complex functions for computational efficiency.
Coordinate transformations (polar, cylindrical, spherical) to simplify multidimensional mathematical problems.
